did_you_know.text: Did you know? Isaiah describes a wondrous transformation in nature: the wilderness and the desert will rejoice, and the wasteland will celebrate and blossom like a crocus.

Did you know? The blossoming of the land is described as great joy—with gladness, singing, and flowers—and it reveals the glory and splendor of the Lord, like the fruitfulness of Lebanon, Carmel, and Sharon.
Did you know? Before describing salvation, the prophet calls for the weak to be strengthened: to strengthen feeble hands and steady trembling knees.
Did you know? Those with anxious hearts are told not to fear, because the Lord will come with vengeance and salvation.
Did you know? Salvation is also described as physical healing: the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped.
Did you know? The chapter says that the lame will leap like a deer and the mute will sing for joy; at that time, water will gush in the wilderness and streams will flow in the desert.
Did you know? Even places of scorching heat and thirst will become pools and springs of water, and vegetation such as reeds and rushes will grow around them.
Did you know? In the wilderness there will be a special road called “the Way of Holiness,” presented as a clear and safe path for those who travel on it.
Did you know? No lion or wild beast will be found on the Way of Holiness, and those who walk on it will be the redeemed and will be safe.
Did you know? The chapter ends by describing the Lord’s redeemed returning to Zion with singing, with everlasting joy crowning their heads; gladness and joy will replace sorrow and sighing.
